descriptionChirho: An interrogative or relative adverb of place asking or indicating the location of something or someone; 'where?' or 'the place where.' Used in direct questions (Mt 2:2; 26:17; Mk 14:12,14; Lk 8:25; 17:17,37; 22:9,11; Jn 1:38; 7:11,35; 8:10,19; 9:12; 11:34; Rev 2:13) and indirect clauses (Jn 3:8; 6:62; 12:1; 20:2,13,15; Heb 11:8; 1 Pet 4:18; 2 Pet 3:4). Translations uniformly render as locative interrogative: eng 'where/Where,' spa 'dónde/Dónde,' arb أَيْنَ (ayna, where), hin कहाँ/कहां (kahan, where), kor 어디에/어디로 (eodie/eodiro, where/whither), swa 'wapi' (where).

An indefinite adverb of place indicating an unspecified or generalized location; 'anywhere' or 'in some place.' This single occurrence (1 Cor 1:2 variant or contextual usage) shifts from the interrogative 'where?' to the indefinite 'in any place.' Translations reflect the indefinite scope: eng 'anywhere,' spa 'en algún lugar' (in some place), arb فِي أَيِّ مَكَانٍ (fi ayyi makanin, in any place), hin ही (emphatic particle signaling generality), kor 어디에서 (eodieseo, in whatever place), swa 'popote' (anywhere/wherever). The indefinite sense arises from πού losing its accent and interrogative force in certain syntactic environments.
